inputs.share_count_basis: 524.52m shares outstanding per the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (24 Jul 2026) plus 4m dilutive RSU/PSU effect per the FY2025 and Q2-2026 diluted-EPS tables (526m diluted weighted average vs 522m basic). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so compounding the count as well would charge dilution twice. No buyback has been executed since the Combination (FY2025 repurchases $0), so the flat count is a modelling convention, not yet funded; management guides buyback capacity from 2027.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Jun 2026 10-Q via SEC XBRL: DebtCurrent 931 + LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations 13,233 = 14,164 total debt (includes ~$550m finance lease liabilities); cash 677. inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation expense $139m (operating) plus $69m tax paid in connection with shares withheld from employees (financing). The company publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. The adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation shows the same $139m expense. H1-2026 10-Q: $55m expense + $85m withholding tax (legacy WestRock replacement awards vesting).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was $111m but is NOT stripped: the company is a large net debtor (net debt ~2.7x EBITDA), so there is no cash pile being double-counted, and the component build starts from Adjusted EBITDA, which already excludes interest income (interest expense, net is an add-back). Recorded here as 0 per the house rule for companies without meaningful net cash.

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate. CAPM: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta 1.1 (observed post-merger beta 0.96, packaging peers IP/PKG historically 1.1-1.2) = Ke ~9.7%; pre-tax Kd 5.2% (Nov-2025 USD green notes 5.185%), ~3.9% after tax; D/V ~38% at the current price (market cap ~$21.8bn, net debt $13.5bn) gives WACC ~7.5%. House figure 8.0%, applied identically to all three scenarios so that cyclical risk is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows, and not again via per-scenario discount rates. Terminal cap multiple 15x FCF (lower end of the house 12-20x band for a cyclical, capital-intensive industrial); at this company's ~37% FCF/EBITDA conversion 15x FCF is only ~5.6x EBITDA, which is below the 6.9x the market pays today and below mature packaging peers at 7-9x -- the required-return table shows what a less conservative exit is worth.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer. Operating leases ($1,095m liability at Dec-2025) are an operating cost inside Adjusted EBITDA and OCF -- treatment (B), excluded from net debt. Finance leases ($550m) sit inside reported debt (Current portion of debt / Non-current debt) and are therefore in total_debt -- treatment (A); the $43m/yr finance-lease principal repayment is NOT deducted from the flows. Each lease class is charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests $24m at 30 Jun 2026, net income attributable to NCI nil in FY2024-25. Deducted once in equity_bridge at book; flows are consolidated.
inputs.pension_note: Prepaid pension asset $616m vs pension and OPEB liabilities $697m at Dec-2025 (funded status +$368m US / -$398m other): net ~-$80m, immaterial at $0.15/share, not bridged. Cash funding exceeded expense by $111m in FY2025, a drag that sits below Adjusted EBITDA and is covered by the 0.5pp owner-margin haircut below.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Smurfit Westrock is a vertically integrated containerboard/corrugated and consumer packaging manufacturer: a stream of unlevered free cash flow is exactly what it produces, so the default engine applies. ENTITY BREAK: FY2016-FY2023 and H1-2024 in the Metrics history are Smurfit Kappa Group standalone (EUR, ~260m shares); the combined Smurfit Westrock (USD, ~520m shares) exists only from 5 Jul 2024, so FY2025 is the first clean full year and is the FY0 revenue base. Pre-merger per-share history is legacy-entity context only. OWNER MARGIN: ebitda_margin_path is the Adjusted EBITDA margin LESS 0.5pp (~$160m/yr) for cash costs Adjusted EBITDA excludes but a serial consolidator incurs every year: FY2025 impairment & restructuring $385m (of which $246m non-cash impairment, ~$140m cash) plus $120m transaction/integration; H1-2026 restructuring & impairment $173m. SBC is then charged separately via sbc_pct_path. MID-CYCLE: FY2026 (guidance $4.9-5.1bn Adjusted EBITDA, ~15.7% margin on ~$31.8bn) is treated as a sub-mid-cycle year -- volumes down 4.8-7.4% in North America, $520m of freight/energy inflation, and the ~$240/ton containerboard price rounds only flowing through from H2 -- so base margins recover toward a 17.5% Adjusted (17.0% owner) mid-cycle level by FY2030, versus Smurfit Kappa standalone's 15-18.5% range in 2016-2023 and management's aspirational ~19.5% (the bull case). Half of FY2026 has elapsed at the June-2026 balance sheet date while the engine treats FY2026 as a full forward year; H1-2026 FCF was -$120m (seasonal), so the overlap is worth under $0.25/share and is ignored.
inputs.fy2026_guidance: Q2-2026 results (29 Jul 2026): FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA $4.9-5.1bn; Q3 ~$1.3bn; capex $2.4-2.5bn; cash interest ~$0.7bn; cash tax ~$0.5bn; ETR ~29%; D&A ~$2.6bn; freight +$300m and energy +$220m vs FY2025. Medium-term plan (Feb 2026): ~$7bn Adjusted EBITDA by 2030 (~7% CAGR, ~300bps margin), ~$13bn capex 2026-30 (~$4bn growth), ~$14bn cumulative discretionary FCF, ~$5bn dividends, buyback capacity from 2027, net debt/EBITDA < 2.0x.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward judgment, not a historical CAGR: medium-term plan market growth (~1.6% North America, ~1.7% Europe, ~2.0% LATAM) plus ~1pp price/mix, decelerating to 2.0% terminal. The historical CAGRs are Smurfit Kappa Group standalone in EUR (FY2016-FY2023) and cannot be compounded from the combined-entity USD base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 15.0% diverges >30% from revenue 4.7% and owner-FCF 4.2%: the legacy entity's book value compounded on retained earnings and the FY2021-22 pricing boom, not on organic volume growth. All CAGRs are legacy Smurfit Kappa (EUR, FY2018-FY2023); the entity changed on 5 Jul 2024.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) for the legacy entity, EUR m: FY2016 292, FY2017 275, FY2018 479, FY2019 508, FY2020 716, FY2021 320, FY2022 505, FY2023 587. The 3yr CAGR to FY2023 is negative because FY2020 was a working-capital-release peak. SBC's share of reported FCF rose from 3.9% (FY2016) to 9.0% (FY2023) and to 17% in the combined entity's FY2025 (208/1200 incl. withholding tax) -- a growing share of reported cash flow is being paid in stock, which is why the house basis charges it. Combined entity FY2024 (half-year of WestRock, USD) owner FCF was -$316m and is not a usable base; FY2025 owner FCF $992m on reported $1,200m. EPS 5yr CAGR is undefined (FY2018 EPS -2.74 after the Venezuela deconsolidation).

base.growth_note: FY2026 +2.0%: H1-2026 net sales +0.9% with the Sep-2026 $100/ton round and earlier increases building in H2. FY2027 +4.0% is the full-year carry of ~$240/ton cumulative containerboard pricing plus a modest volume recovery, then fading to market growth (~1.6-2.0%) + ~0.5pp price/mix. Revenue reaches ~$35.8bn in FY2030, close to the ~$36bn implied by management's $7bn/19.5% plan -- the base case differs from the plan on margin, not revenue.
base.margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA margin 15.7% FY2026 (guidance midpoint $5.0bn on ~$31.8bn) -> 16.5% -> 17.0% -> 17.3% -> 17.5% from FY2030, less the 0.5pp recurring restructuring/integration haircut = owner path shown. 17.5% Adjusted is the midpoint between the FY2026 trough and management's ~19.5% 2030 target and sits inside Smurfit Kappa standalone's FY2019-23 range (17.0-18.5%). Implies ~$6.3bn Adjusted EBITDA in 2030 vs the ~$7bn plan.
base.da_capex_note: D&A ~$2.6bn FY2026 guidance = 8.2% of revenue, drifting to 7.2% as WestRock purchase-accounting step-up amortisation fades. Capex 7.7% FY2026 ($2.45bn, guidance $2.4-2.5bn); FY2026-30 path sums to ~$13.0bn, matching the medium-term plan's ~$13bn (including ~$4bn growth capex). Terminal capex 7.3% vs D&A 7.2%: a capital-intensive mill system does not get to run capex below depreciation.
base.tax_note: Cash tax on unlevered EBIT. Guidance is ~$0.5bn cash tax at a ~29% ETR on LEVERED pre-tax income (~$0.7bn cash interest); the equivalent unlevered rate on EBIT is higher early on because deferred-tax unwinds and non-deductible purchase-accounting amortisation keep cash tax above book tax (FY2025 cash tax $521m vs $260m expense). 32% ramps to the 29% guided ETR by FY2031 as the step-up amortisation rolls off. The interest tax shield is in the after-tax cost of debt inside WACC, not in the flows.
base.wc_note: Receivables $4.9bn + inventories $3.6bn - payables $3.5bn = ~$5.1bn trade working capital at 30 Jun 2026, ~16% of revenue; a manufacturer's growth consumes cash, so capture is NEGATIVE at 10% of the revenue change.

bull.note: The medium-term plan delivered: Adjusted EBITDA margin 16.0% FY2026 (top of guidance) -> 19.5% by FY2030 (owner 19.0%) on ~$37.6bn revenue = ~$7.3bn Adjusted EBITDA, i.e. the ~$7bn target met. Revenue carries two full pricing rounds (FY2027 +5.5%) and a volume recovery as the ~10% US capacity removal holds. Same capex, tax, WACC and terminal assumptions as base so the bull axis is operating delivery alone.

bear.note: Pricing discipline breaks: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance ($4.9bn, 15.4% Adjusted), the 2026 price rounds are given back in FY2027 as Asian exports and restarted capacity meet flat-to-falling box demand, and Adjusted EBITDA margin settles at ~15.5% (owner 15.0%) -- roughly WestRock's standalone level, i.e. the synergies are absorbed by price erosion. Growth capex is cut to hold capex at D&A (7.2%). No refinancing stress is modelled: the bear axis is margin, with leverage amplifying it into equity.

scenario_narratives.base: Smurfit Westrock earns its synergies but not its aspiration. The ~10% of US containerboard capacity removed since Feb-2025 keeps the North American mill system sold out and the 2026 price rounds stick, lifting Adjusted EBITDA from the ~$5.0bn FY2026 guidance midpoint to ~$6.3bn by 2030 (17.5% margin) rather than the ~$7bn plan. Volumes recover only to market growth (~1.6-2%). Capex runs ~$2.5-2.7bn a year, so the ~$13bn 2026-30 envelope is spent in full and the dividend (~$0.95bn/yr) absorbs most of the levered FCF until 2028, keeping buybacks modest. Leverage drifts down toward 2x on EBITDA growth rather than debt paydown. Value is ~55% terminal: this is a mature, capital-intensive mid-cycle compounder, not a growth story.
scenario_narratives.bull: Industry consolidation (IP/DS Smith, SW itself, PCA's pricing lead) has changed containerboard's cycle: capacity discipline holds, a second full pricing round lands in 2027, and box demand turns positive on e-commerce and plastic substitution. Synergies already past $400m plus footprint rationalisation (nine closures, ~500kt) take the Adjusted EBITDA margin to ~19.5% by 2030 -- the medium-term plan's ~$7bn delivered on ~$37.6bn of revenue. Discretionary FCF compounds at the guided ~17% CAGR, buybacks begin in 2027 and the group re-rates toward mature packaging multiples (7-9x EBITDA).
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 pricing recovery proves to be a supply-side pause, not a regime change. Chinese and other Asian exporters redirect excess board into Europe and the Americas, idled US capacity restarts into a soft box market (NA corrugated volumes were -7.4% and -4.8% in Q1/Q2 2026), and the $240/ton of 2026 increases erode through 2027-28. Freight and energy inflation (~$520m in FY2026) is not recovered. Adjusted EBITDA stalls at ~$4.7-5.0bn, margins settle near 15.5% -- WestRock's standalone level -- and with $13.5bn of net debt the equity absorbs the full swing: every 1pp of margin is ~$320m of EBITDA and roughly $3/share of value. Integration (works councils, IT, closures) drags on and restructuring charges keep recurring. Dividend growth stops but no covenant event occurs.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% and bull cut from 35% to 25%. Bear up: $13.5bn of net debt (~2.7x FY2026 EBITDA) turns a cyclical margin miss into an outsized equity move, North American volumes have fallen for two consecutive quarters while prices rose, and management's own 2030 targets are labelled aspirational. Bull down: the bull case needs three independent things to hold at once -- industry pricing discipline, the 2030 margin plan, and a volume recovery -- and the Combination is the largest integration in the sector's history with works councils still merging in Europe. Base at 50% carries the central mid-cycle view.

entry_price.note: With net debt at ~62% of enterprise value, a 15% equity hurdle on unlevered flows discounted from an 8% WACC collapses the entry price to a small fraction of intrinsic value; this is a mechanical property of leverage, not a view that the shares are worth that. Read the required_return_table for the IRR the current price implies.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Smurfit Westrock as a levered, capital-intensive, mid-cycle industrial: unlevered owner FCF built from an Adjusted EBITDA margin that is haircut for recurring restructuring cash and fully charged for stock compensation, discounted at a single USD WACC, with the exit capped at 15x FCF (~5.6x EBITDA, below today's 6.9x). The central question is where the mid-cycle margin sits between the FY2026 trough (~15.7% Adjusted) and management's 2030 plan (~19.5%); the house base answers 17.5%. Leverage does the rest: at $13.5bn of net debt, a 2pp swing in mature margin moves the equity by roughly a third.
key_risks_to_valuation: Containerboard pricing: the model assumes the 2026 rounds stick in base; if they reverse (bear) the equity loses ~half its base value because net debt is fixed while EBITDA is not
Leverage: $14.2bn gross debt, ~$0.7bn cash interest; a 100bp refinancing shock is ~$140m of interest, and the equity bridge deducts net debt at face regardless of scenario
Capex intensity: the ~$13bn 2026-30 envelope (~7.5-7.8% of revenue) is modelled as spent in full; any slippage toward D&A (7.2%) adds value, any mill rebuild overrun removes it
Terminal cap: 15x FCF is ~5.6x EBITDA, well below peers' 7-9x; the valuation is deliberately not relying on a re-rating, and the gap to Gordon (17x FCF at 8%/2%) is shown in the sensitivity grid
Entity and currency break: historical CAGRs are legacy Smurfit Kappa in EUR and cannot be used to compound the USD base; FY2025 is the only clean full year of the combined entity
Quote source: the LSE line (SWR) is inactive since 2026-06-19; the price is the NYSE SW quote in USD, and any price refresh must use the SW symbol
